newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mostly lower despite firm cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mostly lower despite firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended mostly lower Wednesday due to some technical selling shortly before the close when November failed to break through resistance, industry sources said.
November finished a half-cent lower at $2.18 per million British thermal units after some late technical selling. December held onto its gains to settle up 0.4 cent at $2.364.

"Cash was still strong at the end, but people were just covering some shorts. The market is pretty dull," said one trader, noting prices at the New York city-gate were mostly in the mid-to-high $2.20s.
After the $2.22 resistance point, which held through today's session, traders saw the next ceilings in the $2.26-2.28 area and then $2.305. Support was pegged at $2.14, then $2.105 and $2.03.
After trading in only a one-cent range, NYMEX November Alberta natgas ended a half-cent lower on the day at $1.00.
Physical prices at the AECO-C Hub were fairly steady today in the C$1.29-1.30 per gigajoule area.
NYMEX November Permian natgas settled a half-cent higher at $1.87.
Physical gas prices in the basin eased from Tuesday's highs to the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s.
KCBT's November contract finished 1.5 cents lower at $1.94. Deffereds were mixed. The East/West spread widened by one cent to 24 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha held fairly steady today in the mid-$1.80s.
